WITH f AS (SELECT customer, MIN(ordered_at) fo FROM orders GROUP BY customer),
fs AS (SELECT o.customer, MIN(o.store_id) sid, COUNT(DISTINCT o.store_id) n FROM orders o JOIN f ON o.customer=f.customer AND o.ordered_at=f.fo GROUP BY o.customer),
sp AS (SELECT customer, SUM(subtotal) s FROM orders GROUP BY customer)
SELECT st.name, COUNT(*) customers, AVG(sp.s)/100.0 avg_spend, SUM(CASE WHEN n>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ties
FROM fs JOIN sp USING(customer) LEFT JOIN stores st ON st.id=fs.sid GROUP BY st.name ORDER BY customers DESC

args.sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT customer, MIN(ordered_at) fo FROM orders GROUP BY customer),
fs AS (SELECT o.customer, MIN(o.store_id) sid, COUNT(DISTINCT o.store_id) n FROM orders o JOIN f ON o.customer=f.customer AND o.ordered_at=f.fo GROUP BY o.customer),
sp AS (SELECT customer, SUM(subtotal) s FROM orders GROUP BY customer)
SELECT st.name, COUNT(*) customers, AVG(sp.s)/100.0 avg_spend, SUM(CASE WHEN n>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_ties, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE customer IS NULL) nullcust
FROM fs JOIN sp USING(customer) LEFT JOIN stores st ON st.id=fs.sid GROUP BY st.name ORDER BY customers DESC

args.message: Each customer is assigned to the store of their first order. Lifetime spend is the pre-tax total (SUM(subtotal)/100) of all their orders at every store. No customer had a tie for first order. Averages mostly track store age: New Orleans (opened Apr 2025) and Los Angeles (opened Oct 2025) have short customer histories.
